_comment: virp-onode-home device template (node_id 0x0000000D, 10.0.0.13). TRACKED 2026-09-03. Until then this node's fleet existed ONLY as /etc/virp/devices.json on the box: no template, no render step, no unit-manifest row, 38 devices and four plaintext credentials that no commit described. A rebuild would have lost the whole fleet silently. That is the same failure the colo node had with its 43 devices, one node over. Rendered to /run/virp/devices.json at daemon start by deploy/render-devices.sh, substituting ${...} from /etc/virp/autopilot.env (0600 root). This template carries NO credentials.
_credentials_required: autopilot.env on this node must define exactly five values, and render-devices.sh is FATAL on any placeholder it cannot resolve — the daemon refuses to start rather than authenticate as a literal ${TOKEN}. VIRP_PVE_PASSWORD (pve-lab root), VIRP_LABNET_PASSWORD (aiops-svc, shared by all 35 GNS3 routers), VIRP_WAZUH_HOME_PASSWORD (virp-ro on wazuh-home), VIRP_FORTIGATE_HOME_PASSWORD (virp-gate on fortigate-home). Confirmed by hashing every credential in the live config and its eleven backups on 2026-09-03: four distinct values, no more. NOTE the 35 routers share ONE credential — compromise of any one of them is compromise of all thirty-five, which is a property of the lab, recorded here rather than fixed here. FIFTH, added 2026-09-06: VIRP_LABSWITCH1_PASSWORD, the virp-ro TACACS identity for LAB-SWITCH-1 (10.0.0.10). The node also still defines SWITCH_PASS, which this template no longer references after that switch moved to virp-ro -- it is left in place rather than removed here, because autopilot.env is node state and dropping a live credential is a separate, deliberate act.
_socket_allowlist_policy: uid 0 is EXCLUDED, same as the colo node: a client running as root is rejected at the peercred gate. 999 is the daemon's own service account, 1000 the interactive operator, 997 virp-spark (the Spark's requester identity), 1001 virp-laptop (the laptop approver identity, reaching the socket over a forwarded stream).
_socket_uid_action_allow_note: FIXES A LIVE DEPLOY BLOCKER (Phase 0 D4). Until 2026-09-03 only 997 and 1001 had action maps; 999 and 1000 were allowlisted with NO entry, which this node's binary treats as unrestricted and origin/main treats as a boot failure. Both now have one, and 999 loses the shutdown it implicitly held. EIGHT VERBS EACH, NOT TWENTY, AND THE NUMBER IS LOAD-BEARING: ONODE_MAX_UID_ACTIONS is 8 in the binary this node runs and only became 32 in 13ec426 (2026-09-01) — the very commit that added the boot invariant. A longer list overflows the cap and virp_onode_prod.c fails closed by installing DENY-ALL for that uid, which is what happened on the first attempt here: 'uid 999 action allowlist: 0 action(s) (DENY-ALL)', reverted. So the colo node's 20-verb list is NOT portable to this node, and copying it here was the mistake. Eight is also simply the better answer: this node runs no comparator, no netclaw bridge and no v2 sessions, so the session_*, intent_*, batch_execute and validate_turn verbs it was granted were reach nothing here uses. Expanding past 8 becomes possible after the binary upgrade and should be justified by a workload, not by symmetry with virp-lab.
_socket_uid_chain_append_types_note: Second half of the same blocker: absent entirely on this node until now. A uid whose action set includes chain_append MUST appear here or the daemon refuses to start naming it. Only 999 and 1000 may chain_append; 997 and 1001 have no chain_append verb and correctly have no entry. `evidence_item` is present so the deployed-state reporter can land its document as a real body rather than a commitment-only hash every reader would grade UNVERIFIABLE — see the matching note in deploy/devices.template.json. Types use the 16-byte-truncated spellings the wire delivers.
_gate_posture_note: gate_max_tier is GREEN here, tighter than the colo node's YELLOW, and deliberately unchanged by this file. pve-lab has NO Proxmox classifier, so its commands land RED-by-absence and are proposal-only and fail-closed. Tracking a config is not the moment to change what it permits: this template is byte-for-byte the posture the node was already running, plus the two policy objects whose ABSENCE was the bug.
_socket_uid_992_note: 992 = virp-tacacs, the TACACS+ accounting receiver (session 5, 2026-09-05). ONE verb, chain_append, and nothing else: the receiver never executes, never reads a device and never holds a device credential -- it decodes accounting packets from a switch and lands them as evidence. One verb is also well under ONODE_MAX_UID_ACTIONS, which is 8 in the binary this node runs; see the action_allow note above for why that number is load-bearing. The append type is evidence_item because artifact_type is char[16] (15 usable) and tacacs_accounting is 17 -- the real type rides as the body schema tacacs_accounting/1, the same shape every external producer here uses. All three of allowed_uids/action_allow/chain_append_types were added in ONE edit deliberately: a uid carrying chain_append with no append-type entry does NOT degrade to a refused append, it stops the daemon booting, which on this node is an outage across 38 governed devices. The tier ceiling is inert (992 has no execute verb) and present only so every allowlisted uid is described.
_socket_uid_993_note: 993 = virp-netclaw, the remote requester identity for netclaw/Nexus (10.0.30.30), added 2026-09-05 so the agents can observe the home segment through this node's gate instead of reaching its devices. Same number as virp-netclaw on virp-lab (.211), chosen because 993 was free here and already means exactly this there -- the one uid that converges the two nodes' spaces rather than adding to the collision debt recorded in deploy/FLEET-UIDS.md. FOUR VERBS: list_fleet, health, execute, chain_verify. No chain_append, and therefore deliberately NO socket_uid_chain_append_types entry -- the boot invariant requires an append-type policy only for a uid that carries chain_append, and this one must not. Four is well under ONODE_MAX_UID_ACTIONS (8 on this node's binary; see the action_allow note above for why that number is load-bearing). Ceiling is green, and this node's gate_max_tier is green node-wide, so nothing this identity submits can execute above GREEN by either path. The account MUST exist before this template is rendered: render-devices.sh resolves ${VIRP_NETCLAW_UID} with pwd.getpwnam('virp-netclaw') and is FATAL if it cannot, which stops the daemon booting across 38 governed devices. Create the user first, render second.

devices._comment: Wazuh manager. protected_agents are refused by the driver at any tier and classify VIRP_TIER_BLACK at the gate hook, so the refusal files no proposal and no approval reaches it. Enforced on the endpoint bytes, NOT via the API credential's RBAC: Wazuh denies at resource level with HTTP 200 and the agent simply absent from affected_items, which is indistinguishable from the agent not existing.
devices._tls_note: Running on the lab insecure drop-in (VIRP_WAZUH_INSECURE=1) pending cert reissue. The manager presents the stock self-signed cert (CN=wazuh.com, only SAN DNS:localhost), so addressing it by IP cannot pass hostname verification even with that cert trusted as a CA. Fix is to reissue the API cert with IP:10.0.0.44 in the SAN and point VIRP_CA_BUNDLE at its signer, then remove the drop-in.

devices._comment: LAB-SWITCH-1 -- the lab Catalyst 2960 (WS-C2960-24TC-L, IOS 12.2(55)SE6, C2960-LANBASEK9-M). Added 2026-09-05 for the TACACS+ accounting work, read-only by construction. ssh_legacy=true IS REQUIRED AND WAS TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: this train offers exactly one KEX, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, and nothing else. A handshake-only libssh2 probe run on this node against the live switch failed with CISCO_KEX_DEFAULT (rc=-5, 'Unable to exchange encryption keys' -- the same refusal OpenSSH gives) and succeeded with CISCO_KEX_LEGACY, negotiating kex=diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 hostkey=ssh-rsa crypt=aes256-cbc and offering keyboard-interactive,password, both of which driver_cisco.c implements. The weak algorithms are the switch's ceiling, not a preference; ssh_legacy is per-device so it lowers nothing for the other 38. No 'enable' credential: aiops-svc is priv 15 and the no-enable refusal in virp_onode_prod.c is cisco_asa-only. The password RODE ${SWITCH_PASS} until 2026-09-06 -- see CREDENTIAL CHANGED at the end of this comment -- which was a DISTINCT value from VIRP_LABNET_PASSWORD (digests 40ca091e vs 0db9c95d, compared 2026-09-05) and therefore a NEW entry in this node's autopilot.env -- render-devices.sh lists SWITCH_PASS in its required-vars tuple and is FATAL when the template names a placeholder the env does not define, so a missing value here stops the daemon booting across every governed device, it does not degrade to one unreachable switch. Secret first, template second. NOTE 12.2(55) has no '| section' filter -- use '| include' / '| begin' -- and no 'tacacs server <name>' block; legacy 'tacacs-server host ... key ...' syntax applies on this train. CREDENTIAL CHANGED 2026-09-06: this row now authenticates as virp-ro via ${VIRP_LABSWITCH1_PASSWORD}, replacing aiops-svc/${SWITCH_PASS}. virp-ro is the TACACS identity served by tac_plus-ng on CT 215, so every gate read of this switch is now authenticated AND per-command authorized there, and lands in that server's decision log -- which is the whole point: one command described by a gate observation here, an accounting receipt here, and an authorization decision on 215. THIS IS FAIL-CLOSED BY DESIGN: if CT 215 is unreachable the gate cannot read this switch at all. That is intended per docs/TACACS-ACCOUNTING.md 9.1 -- gate identities have no local fallback, and humans reach the box by console, which is exempt. ${SWITCH_PASS} is no longer referenced by this template; it remains defined in this node's autopilot.env and in render-devices.sh's tuple, where it still names cat3850-lab on the COLO node. virp-ro is priv 1, below aiops-svc's priv 15, and the GREEN table needs nothing above priv 1.
